paragraphs: Kol hannashim yesh lahem veset qabua: yesh roa kol sheloshim yom, veyesh roa kol esrim vachamishsha yom vekayyotze bazeh. veameru baggemara: vehizzartem et bene-yisrael mittumatam" - amar rab yoshiyyahu: mikkan azhara libne-yisrael sheyyipreshu minneshotehen samuk levistan, vekamma? amar raba: ona. vehaoneh hi yom o hallayla – sheim vistah ballayla, ap-al-pi shergila lirot sop hallayla, tzarik liprosh mimmenna mittechillat hallayla. veyesh omerim deona zo hi lipne haona shehusat bah, dehaynu, im vistah bayyom, tzarik liprosh mimmenna kol hallayla shellepanayv. umaran za"l sebira lah kaddea harishona, ak tzarik lachush ledea zo hashsheniyya, biprat beyamim elleh shehaggupim hem chalushim.

clarification.explanation: Every woman has some fixed cycle (veset) — some see it every thirty days, some every twenty-five days, and so on. Our Sages derived from the verse "and you shall separate the children of Israel from their impurity" that a married couple is obligated to separate from each other close to the time of the veset, and according to the Gemara the duration of separation is an "onah" — that is, a full day or a full night. If her veset falls at night, one must separate from the start of the night, even if she is normally accustomed to seeing it only at the end. There is a further opinion that one must separate already during the onah preceding the veset's actual time (for example, if her veset is during the day, one should separate the entire preceding night), and although the halacha follows the first opinion, one should be concerned for the second opinion as well, especially in generations of weaker constitution.
takeaways: One must separate from one's wife for a full onah (a day or a night) close to her fixed veset time.
If the veset is at night, one separates from its very start; one should also be concerned to separate already during the preceding onah.

paragraphs: Happarasha zo hi davqa mittashmish-hammitta, abal shear qerebot en tzarik liprosh; mihu, mechibbuq venishshuq tzarik liprosh - meachar deasur lo labo aleha, ek yaaseh chibbuq venishshuq vigareh beatzmo taavat hayyetzer? veshomer napsho yirchaq mizzeh! veken im darko lishon immah bime tahoratah bekar vesadin echad, hinneh kol heka devistah ballayla, lo yishan immah bekar echad, ki shemma tireh betok shena velo targish ella ad or habboqer, venimtza hu yashen immah beqarob bihyotah poreset nidda, laken tzarik lehizzaher bazeh.

clarification.explanation: The separation required close to the veset concerns specifically marital relations themselves, but not other bodily closeness. Nevertheless, embracing and kissing are also forbidden during that same onah — since it is forbidden to be intimate with her, there is no logic in drawing close to her in a manner that would arouse desire, and a person guarding his soul should distance himself from this. Likewise, if they are accustomed to sleeping together on one pillow and sheet during her days of purity, one must be careful: on any night the veset falls, one should not sleep with her on one pillow, lest she see blood during sleep and not notice until morning, and it would turn out he slept with her close to the time she became a niddah.
takeaways: The separation close to the veset applies to marital relations, but also to embracing and kissing — so as not to arouse desire.
On the night the veset falls, one should not sleep with the woman on one pillow, out of concern she might see blood without noticing.

paragraphs: Im nishtanna vistah, dehaynu, haya vistah lirot kol sheloshim yom, veshinneta veraata yom k"ch o k"t, az achar shettitbol min hareiyya shel veset zeh sheshshinneta bo, tzerika lachush bappaam hazzot leveset hashshinnuy shehu yom k"ch o yom k"t, vetiprosh bahem mittashmish; dechayeshinan shemma gam bappaam hazzot tireh beyom k"ch o beyom k"t; veken hu haddin im hashshinnuy haya leachor, dehaynu sheshshinneta lirot yom l" o yom l"g.

clarification.explanation: If a woman's veset changed — for example it was normally every thirty days, and once she saw earlier, on day twenty-eight or twenty-nine — then after she immerses from this new occurrence, she must be concerned the next time also for the "veset of the change" itself (day twenty-eight or twenty-nine) and separate from relations on that day too, out of concern she might again see on that same day. The same law applies if the change went in the opposite direction — that is, she saw later, on day thirty-one or thirty-three.
takeaways: If the veset changed (earlier or later than usual), one must be concerned also for the new day she saw, in addition to the original veset.
This applies whether the change was earlier or later.

paragraphs: Ishah sheriyyatah nimsheket b' o g' d' yamim, shehi shopaat o mazlepet bahem - hinneh sebarat maran za"l deyom hatchalat reiyyatah hu haiqqar shetztzerika lachush lo liprosh mittashmish, vekivvun sheabera ona velo raata, mutteret. vekatab harab "lechem vesimla", dedaat haraaba"d veharamba"n dechosheshet lekol yeme meshek havveset, shekkol yom veyom veset bipne atzmo hu; velaken apillu neeqar yom harishon, chosheshet lishar hayyamim ad sheyyeaqeru kullam, veyesh lachush ledibrehem, ad kan; veken iqqar deyesh lachush ledibrehem; mihu im abera veshimmesha bahem veara taqqala shennitmet bishat tashmish, eno niddon kemi shebba al ishto bishat vistah; venapeqa maneh tuba leinyan hattiqqun shetztzarik laasot lazeh haissur.

clarification.explanation: A woman whose flow (bleeding) continues for two, three, or four days, whether heavy or spotting — according to Maran, only the day the bleeding began is the determining factor requiring separation from relations, and since that onah has passed without her seeing again, she is permitted. However, according to the Ra'avad and the Ramban, who carry halachic weight, one must be concerned for all the days of the flow's duration — each day is considered a veset in its own right, and therefore even if the first day was uprooted (did not recur), one must still be concerned for the remaining days until all of them are uprooted. If nevertheless relations occurred on these days and an impurity mishap occurred during the act, this is not considered like one who had relations with his wife during her actual veset, and this has implications for the nature of the required atonement.
takeaways: With a multi-day flow, one must be concerned (according to the Ra'avad and Ramban) for every day of the flow's duration as its own veset, not just the first day.
If a mishap occurred during relations on these days, its severity is lighter than relations during an actual veset.

paragraphs: Ishsha sheen lah veset qabua, az sheloshim sheachar reiyyatah hu lah veset qabua, vetzarik liprosh mittashmish. vekol ishsha sheyyesh lah veset qabua, eno neeqar ella beshalosh peamim; vehamubberet, leachar shelosha chodashim mittechillat ibburah, veken hammeniqa enan chosheshin leveset. vetizzaher haishsha shello tirchatz beyom zeman havveset haqqabua lah, dechosheshin shemma orach bizmanno ba, veyered birchitza velo hirgisha.

clarification.explanation: A woman with no fixed veset — the thirtieth day after her occurrence is considered for her a fixed veset, and she must separate from relations on it. A fixed veset is uprooted (ceases to be considered fixed) only after three times it fails to recur. A pregnant woman, after three months from the start of pregnancy, and likewise a nursing woman, need no longer be concerned about a veset. One should be careful that a woman not bathe on her fixed veset day, lest the bleeding come at its time and be washed away in the bath without her noticing it.
takeaways: With no fixed veset — the thirtieth day after an occurrence is considered a fixed veset.
A fixed veset is uprooted only after three times it fails to recur; a pregnant woman (from the third month) and a nursing woman need not be concerned about a veset.
One should not bathe on the fixed veset day, lest the bleeding be washed away unnoticed.

paragraphs: Kalla sheera tebilatah belel chuppatah baona shehusat bah, "p shezzo habbeila harishona "beilat" metzuvveh qaryuha rabbanan, apillu hake asur labo aleha beoto hallayla; vaapillu im vistah hu besop hallayla vehu meshammesh bitchillat hallayla, name asur, vekaasher hora haggaon "noda bihuda", mahdura batera, siman qy"ch.

clarification.explanation: A bride whose immersion falls on her wedding night exactly at the time of her veset — even though the first union is called by our Sages "a union of mitzvah" — it is forbidden for her husband to be intimate with her that night, even if her veset falls at the end of the night and he has relations at its beginning.
takeaways: Even a "union of mitzvah" on the wedding night is forbidden if the bride's veset time falls then, even at the beginning of the night when the veset is only at its end.

paragraphs: Kol ishah enah nitheret lebaalah ella im ken tispor techilla z' neqiyyim, vaapillu raata tippat dam kechardal. veenah yekola limnot z' neqiyyim velitbol ella davqa im aberu aleha shishsha yamim miyyom sheraata bo; veyesh machmirim achar z' yamim, vekol echad yaaseh keminhago bazeh. upoh irenu bagdad, rob hair minhagam limnot achar shishsha yamim, ak yesh mishpachot shemminhagam achar shiba yamim; al-ken, ishah asher mishpachtah nohagim limnot z' neqiyyim achar shiba yamim, vehi min paam rishona shennisset rotza linhog keotam mishpachot denahagu achar shishsha, yekola lemebad hake, kevan dela nahaga adayin kammachmirin. veim yesh ishah shennahaga kebar kammachmirin, veatta mitcharetet mechamat sibbot hekrechiyyut - yekola laasot hattara al minhag shellah beshiba, vetinhag achar shishsha; mihu, baalah lo yesheb im hammattirin lehattir lah.

clarification.explanation: A woman is not purified for her husband until she counts seven clean days (with no bleeding at all, even a mustard-seed-sized drop of blood). She may begin counting and immerse only after six days have passed from the day of the occurrence; some are stringent and wait until after seven days, and each follows their family's custom. In Baghdad most of the public follows the practice of counting after six days, though some families follow seven. A woman whose family is stringent with seven, but who wishes, from her own first marriage, to follow the lenient practice (six) — may do so, since she has not yet personally followed the stringent practice. And one who has already followed the stringent practice and now wishes, for compelling reasons, to revert — may perform a "hatarah" (release from a vow/custom) on her practice, and then follow the lenient practice; but her husband should not sit among those granting the release at the time of the hatarah.
takeaways: Counting seven clean days may begin from the sixth or seventh day after the occurrence, according to family custom (in Baghdad, most follow after six).

A newly married woman may choose the lenient practice if her husband's family has not yet followed it; one who has already followed the stringent practice may perform a hatarah to switch to the lenient one, though her husband should not sit among those granting the release.

paragraphs: Kol zeh - beroa dam nidda, shehirgisha bo sheyyetze; abal im raata ketem al begadeha, tispor z' neqiyyim achar sheaberu aleha chamishsha yamim miyyom shemmatzea hakketem al begadeha. veken hu haddin kalla shennitmet bedam betulim velo parsa nidda, day lah bachamishsha yamim kedin hakketem; abal im zo hakkalla parsa nidda gam ken, dinah kishar niddot dealema, shessoperet achar shishsha o achar shiba keminhag hammachmirin.

clarification.explanation: All the above applies when the woman actually felt blood emerge from her. But if she only found a stain on her clothing (without feeling it), she counts seven clean days already after only five days have passed from the day the stain was found. The same law applies to a bride who became impure only from virginal blood without becoming an actual niddah — five days suffice for her, as with a stain. But if the bride also became a niddah (saw regular bleeding), her law is like any other niddah — she counts after six or seven according to her custom.
takeaways: A stain (not felt) requires only five days before counting seven clean days, compared to six or seven for felt blood.
Virginal blood alone (without becoming a niddah) likewise requires only five days; but if she became a niddah, her law is the regular one.

paragraphs: Otam shennahagu lehachmir lispor z' neqiyyim achar shiba liriyyatam - im nizdammen tebilatam belel yv"t sheni o beshabbat shelleachar yv"t, vetihyeh rechoqa hattebila min hachapipa harbeh, az tukal otah happaam laasot keotam shennohagim lispor achar shishsha, kede shettebul beereb yv"t achar hachapipa tekep; ken taaseh beotah happaam davqa shennizdammen kak, veenah tzerika hattara al minhag shello shennahaga achar shiba, kevan deenah osa ken ella raq beotah happaam shennizdammen kak; veayyen "teshuba meahaba", cheleq b, vekaasher katabti bs"d bsh"q "mqbtzl". vekatabti od: im zo haishsha hannoheget lispor shiba neqiyyim achar shiba liriyyatah, nizdammena tebilatah lel-shabbat, veim titbol mukrach lehikkashel bekamma issurim shel qeliat sear vekayyotze, ki hi ishah chadasha umukrachat lehitqashshet bipne baalah bazeh ubekayyotze bazeh bidbarim sheyyesh bahem chillul shabbat, veim tispor achar shishsha liriyyatah, tihyeh tebilatah belel-shishshi shehu chol - muttar lah lispor otah happaam davqa et shiba neqiyyim achar shishsha liriyyatah.

clarification.explanation: Those who follow the stringent practice of counting seven clean days after seven days from the occurrence — if their immersion happens to fall on the night of the second day of a Festival or the following Sabbath, and the hair-washing (before immersion) is very far removed from the immersion itself — may, on that one occasion only, follow the lenient practice (after six), so they can immerse on the eve of the Festival close to the hair-washing, and they do not need a "hatarah" on their practice since this is a one-time exception. Likewise, a woman who follows the stringent practice, if her immersion falls on Sabbath night and she would be forced to violate Sabbath prohibitions (such as braiding hair required to look presentable for her husband as a new bride), may, on that one occasion only, count according to the lenient practice (after six) so her immersion falls on Friday night, which is a weekday.
takeaways: Those following the stringent practice (seven) may follow the lenient practice (six) on a one-time basis if circumstances (a Festival, the Sabbath, Sabbath prohibitions) require it, without needing a formal release of their custom.

paragraphs: Qodem sepirat z' neqiyyim tzerika laasot hepseq betahora, dehaynu: beyom shishshi liriyyatah, o beyom shebii lehammachmirim, tzerika leet ereb libdoq atzmah bemok dachuq, vattilbash lebanim uneqiyyim. uminhag kasher lirchotz kol gupah bemayim chammin qodem hepseq betahora; veim lo epshar lah, az day shettirchatz panim shel matta bilbad.

clarification.explanation: Before beginning the count of the seven clean days, one must perform a "hefsek taharah" (a cessation-check for purity) — a self-examination with cotton wool (soft cloth) inserted internally, at the end of the sixth day from the occurrence (or the seventh, for those who are stringent), and afterward one should wear white, clean clothing. It is a good custom to wash the entire body in hot water before the hefsek taharah; one who cannot should at least wash the lower part of the body.
takeaways: Hefsek taharah: an internal examination with cotton wool at the end of the sixth or seventh day, followed by wearing white clothing.
It is preferable to wash the entire body beforehand; if not possible, at least the lower part.

paragraphs: Zeman bediqa zo shel hepseq betahora, hu chatzi shaa qodem qeriat ha"magreb", sheqqore besop shaa y"b mammash. veim haishsha hi darkah lehitpallel, tzerika laasot hepseq betahora qodem shettitpallel arbit; sheim hitpallela arbit - enah yekola laasot hepseq betahora, veken im hidliqa nerot shabbat o yv"t - enah yekola laasot hepseq betahora, "p sheod hayyom gadol.

clarification.explanation: The time for the hefsek taharah examination is half an hour before the call of "maghreb" (the sign of sunset). A woman accustomed to praying must perform the hefsek taharah before the evening prayer — since after she has prayed the evening service, or after lighting Sabbath or Festival candles, she can no longer perform the hefsek taharah, even though it is still broad daylight (that is, accepting the Sabbath/Festival or the evening prayer establishes that night has already begun for her, even though in fact it is still daylight).
takeaways: The hefsek taharah is performed half an hour before sunset ("maghreb").
The evening prayer or lighting Sabbath/Festival candles blocks performing the hefsek taharah afterward, even though it is still day.

paragraphs: Haoseh hepseq betahora bemok dachuq beoto maqom, tzarik sheyyihyeh munnach hammok beoto maqom kol ben-hashshemashot ad sheyyihyeh vadday layla; velo keotam burim shemmaknisin hammok bishat bediqa umotziin oto tekep, ella tzarik sheyyishshaer munnach sham, veachar sheyyihyeh vadday layla, az totzi et hammok mishsham vetatzniennu bequpesa ad habboqer, kede shettibdeqehu leor hayyom; ukemo shekkatab rama" za"l behaggahat hashshulchan, siman qp"v, seip b, bebodeqet et haedim achar tashmish; ukemo shekkatab rashi"y za"l benidda, dap t"z, vehattosapot sham bedibbur hammatchil "ema", ayyen sham; yaan kevan dehi motzia oto achar sheyyihyeh vadday layla, choshek hayyom, vei epshar lebadeqo leor hayyom, vegam leor hanner en libdoq lekattechilla, ukemo shekkatab mera"n bebet yosep, siman qtz"v, vehebio mvr"m behaggahat hashshulchan, seip d, yeuyyan sham; vetzarik lehazhir hannashim bedabar zeh, lehannicha hammok beoto maqom kol ben-hashshemashot ad vadday layla. veap al gab demera"n za"l hittir bediabad im hotzia oto miyyad, im kol zeh modeh dilkattechilla tzarik lehizzaher bazeh; veod dehaggaon "sidre-tahora" heela middibre haramba"m za"l vekamma rabbevata daapillu bediabad meakkeb.

clarification.explanation: One who performs the hefsek taharah with the cotton wool inserted internally must leave the cotton wool in place throughout the entire twilight period until it is certainly night — not as the mistaken custom of those who insert the cotton wool and remove it immediately. Once night is certain, she removes the cotton wool and puts it away in a box until morning, in order to examine it by daylight (since an examination in darkness, even by candlelight, is not proper as the primary practice). Women should be especially warned about this matter. Although after the fact, if she removed the cotton wool immediately, it is valid, as the primary practice one should leave it until night is certain, and according to some authorities even after the fact this is invalid.
takeaways: The hefsek taharah cotton wool should remain in place until night is certain, and only then removed and put away for examination by daylight the next morning.
After the fact, if removed immediately, some are lenient, but as the primary practice one should insist on leaving it until night is certain.

paragraphs: Bekol yom mishshiba neqiyyim tibdoq paamayim, achat beshacharit veachat samuk leben-hashshemashot; ubediabad im badeqa raq beyom rishon ubayyom hashshebii, saggi lah; ak bediqa shel hepseq betahora lo toil lehashlim bead bediqa shel yom rishon, ella tzerika libdoq beyom rishon millebad bediqa shel hepseq betahora. vehinneh poh irenu bagdad y" yesh harbeh nashim nohagin dela abedi bediqa bekol yom kaasher katabnu, ella abedi beyom rishon ubayyom hashshebii. vekatabti bs"d bsh"q "rab-pealim" deyesh lahem al mah sheyyismoku; abal rauy shekkol adam yazhir et ishto shettibdoq bekol yom kaamur leel. veotam burim sheen osim bediqa beyom rishon ubayyom hashshebii, ella raq somekin al habbediqa shel hepseq betahora lebad, atidin litten et haddin veoy lahem!

clarification.explanation: On each of the seven clean days, one must examine twice — once in the morning and once close to twilight. After the fact, if she examined only on the first and seventh days, this suffices; but the hefsek taharah examination itself cannot serve as a substitute for the first day's examination — the first day must also be examined separately. In Baghdad many women were accustomed to examine only on the first and seventh days, and they have grounds to rely upon, but it is proper for everyone to warn his wife to examine every day as stated. One who performs no examination at all on the first and seventh days, relying only on the hefsek taharah alone — will have to answer for it.
takeaways: One should examine twice daily throughout the seven clean days; after the fact, examining only the first and seventh days suffices.
The hefsek taharah is not a substitute for the first day's examination — it must be examined separately.
Relying only on the hefsek taharah with no examination at all on the first and seventh days is invalid and serious.

paragraphs: Im achar shessippera z' neqiyyim shelemim karauy, naasa lah ones velo tabela lel ch', venitachara tebilatah arbaa o chamishsha lelot - day lah beotah shiba neqiyyim sheshshemarah otam bishlemut vikola litbol; veayyen sha"k, siman qp"z, seip qatan ch', ayyen sham. velav davqa nitachara arbaa o chamishsha lelot, ella apillu im nitachara yoter, yekola litbol al semak otam hashshiba neqiyyim, deken katab haramba"m za"l bepereq d mehilkot issure bia, halaka z': apillu nitachara yamim rabbim velo tabela, keshettitbol, lo titbol ella ballayla.

clarification.explanation: If, after properly counting seven clean days, she was prevented by circumstances beyond her control from immersing on the eighth night, and her immersion was delayed by four or five nights — the seven clean days she kept suffice, and she may immerse. And this is not only when the delay is four or five nights, but even if delayed longer than that — she may still immerse based on the seven clean days she properly kept.
takeaways: A delay in immersion (of any length) does not invalidate seven clean days already properly counted — she may immerse based on them.

paragraphs: Kol bediqot ellu - ben bediqat hepseq betahora, ben bediqa shebbeshiba yamim neqiyyim - tzarik lihyot betzemer-gepen o bebeged pishtan laban yashan, ki pishtan hayyashan hu laban beyoter min pishtan hechadash; veod, ki hechadash qasheh veen haddam nidbaq bo; veod, mittok shehu qasheh, chosheshet shemma yissarek, veenah bodeqet bo yapeh. upoh irenu bagdad, kol hannashim darkan libdoq betzemer-gepen. vetzarik shettaknisennu yapeh beomeq bachorim ubassedaqim ad maqom shehashshammash dash; ubediabad im badeqa yapeh bachorin ubisdaqin beomeq kepi kochah, "p shello higgia lemaqom shehashshammash dash, saggi lah. vehabbetulot shebbodeqot qodem nissuin, depitchan satum vei epshar libdoq ad maqom shehashshammash dash, yibdequ yapeh kepi mah sheepshar; abal qinnucha bealema en zeh bediqa; veayyen "chakemat-adam" v"chinnuk-bet-yeuddeh" v"machatzit-hashsheqel" veod.

clarification.explanation: All the examinations (both the hefsek taharah and the examinations of the seven clean days) must be done with cotton wool, or with old white linen cloth — since old white linen is more absorbent than new, and also because new cloth is stiff and does not absorb blood well, and might stick together such that the examination is not proper. In Baghdad it is customary to examine with cotton wool. The cloth should be inserted well and deeply into all the folds and crevices, to the place "the sun tramples" (a deep place). After the fact, if she examined as well as she could in depth even without reaching the place "the sun tramples," this suffices. Virgins examining before marriage, whose opening is closed and who cannot reach this depth, should examine as best they can — but a mere wipe is not considered an examination.
takeaways: Examinations should be done with cotton wool or old white linen, inserted as deeply as possible.
After the fact, the maximum depth she can reach suffices; a mere wipe is not considered an examination.

paragraphs: Im sapera shiba neqiyyim vetabela karauy, veachar shebbaa lebetah veyasheba im baalah, parsa nidda beotah layla qodem sheshshimmesha im baalah - hare zo poseqet betahora leyom hammachorat, vetimneh shiba neqiyyim vetitbol, veen tzerika lehamtin chamishsha yamim qodem sepirat z' neqiyyim, vekaasher hora geber haggaon "pene-yehoshua" za"l, kevan dela shimmesha adayin; veap-al-gab dibalema anachnu machmirim belo shimmesha, degazerinan attu shimmesha, mikkol maqom bikhay gavna dehu milleta dela shekicha shettipros nidda belel tebilatah - la gazerinan; vela baenan chamishsha yamim qodem z' neqiyyim, kevan daadayin lo shimmesha; udelo kehaggaon noda bihuda, mahadura tinyana, siman qk"h, dehitzrik chamishsha yamim; deha kamma geonim, verabbane ashkenaz useparad hiskimu kisbarat haggaon "pene-yehoshua". veayyen "sidre-tahora" v"bet-meir" v"chakemat-adam", veayyen od leharab "teshuba-meahaba" veod acharonim, veken anachnu morin. veim taata beminyan hashshiba shello hayu ella shishsha, vetabela veshimmesha im baalah, venoda lah shechaser yom echad - tzerika lehamtin shesh onot shelemot, dehaynu arbaa yamim im hayyom shettabela bo, veaach"k timneh yom naqi asher chaser lah, vetitbol; ak setira shel achar shiba, kegon shessapera z' neqiyyim shelemim vetabela tebila pesula, hen mechamat chatzitza o pissul acher, "p sheshshimmesha im baalah enah tzerika lehamtin shesh onot, ella tobelet tebila shenit karauy bekol layla shettirtzeh, deha kebar sapera z' neqiyyim shelemim, raq shehiyyatah mechusseret tebila shello tabela karauy.

clarification.explanation: If she counted seven clean days and immersed properly, and after returning home and sitting with her husband, she saw niddah bleeding that same night before having relations with him — she performs a "hefsek taharah" for the following day, and counts seven clean days and immerses, without needing to wait five days before beginning to count (as with a regular occurrence), since she has not yet had relations with her husband — so ruled the Gaon "Pnei Yehoshua," and not according to the stringent opinion requiring five days even in this case. If she erred in the count of the seven (actually counting only six) and already immersed and had relations, and afterward the deficiency became clear to her — she must wait six full onot (four days including the immersion day), and then count the missing clean day and immerse. However, if the "flaw" was only in the immersion itself (such as an interposition) after a proper and complete count of seven clean days, there is no need to wait six onot — she simply immerses again validly on any night she wishes, since she has already completed the count.
takeaways: Seeing niddah bleeding on the immersion night, before the first union, does not require a new five-day wait before recounting.
An error in counting (counting six by mistake, having already had relations) requires waiting six full onot before completing the missing day.
A flaw in the immersion alone (not the count) requires no waiting — simply immersing again suffices.

paragraphs: "g diktib(vayyiqra tv,kch) "vesapera lah" v"haagudda" ushela"h sebira lehu tzerika lispor bappeh, mikkol maqom rabbim chillequ bazeh usebira lehu bemachshaba saggi, veken amma debar; ak shiba sepurim gemurim bedatah baenan, abal im hitchila lispor bedatah z' neqiyyim ubeemtza chazera bah, sheala bedatah shello litbol mechamat ezeh sibba, kegon shebbalah ratza lelek lemaqom acher, o shennitqoteta im balah vehaleka lebet abiha, veachar b' o g' yamim batela hassibba vegamera bedatah litbol – batelu otam miqtzat hashshiba shessippera miqqodem, utzerika lispor shiba mechadash.

clarification.explanation: Although it is written "and she shall count for herself," and some authorities (the "Agudah" and the "Shelah") hold that one must count aloud, many disagreed and hold that counting in one's mind suffices, and this is the accepted custom. Nevertheless, a complete and clear count in her mind is required for all seven days — if she began counting mentally and in the middle changed her mind (for example, deciding not to immerse for some reason, such as a quarrel with her husband or traveling elsewhere), and only after two or three days changed her mind again and decided to immerse after all — the days she counted before are voided, and she must count seven days anew.
takeaways: Counting the seven clean days may be done mentally, not aloud, but must be continuous and complete in her mind.
A mental interruption (deciding not to immerse, then reconsidering) voids the prior count and requires recounting from the start.

paragraphs: Ishah shemmekina atzmah lenissuin, tzerika lispor z' neqiyyim, mishshum dam chimmud - ben shehi qetanna daadayin lo raata dam nidda, ben shehi zeqena sheppaseqa millirot; utzerika libdoq beshiba neqiyyim ellu kemo beshiba neqiyyim shel dam nidda, ki hecheziqu otah chaza"l kemo nidda mammash. veim sapera z' neqiyyim venidchu hannissuin mechamat ezeh sibba, veaach"k nitpashsheru venitratztzu laasot hannissuin, tzerika lispor z' neqiyyim mechadash, mippene shennolad lah chimmud chadash. umachazir gerushato, gam ken tzerika lispor z' neqiyyim, apillu gereshah keshehi meubberet o meniqa, vehechezirah beodah meubberet, ditzrika z' neqiyyim mishshum chimmud.

clarification.explanation: A woman preparing for her marriage must count seven clean days due to "blood of excitement" (concern for bleeding caused by the excitement of the marriage), whether she is a minor who has never yet seen niddah blood, or an elderly woman who has already ceased seeing it — and her law is that of actual seven clean days of niddah, since our Sages considered her a complete niddah for this purpose. If she counted these seven clean days and the marriage was postponed for some reason, and afterward they reconciled and agreed again to marry — she must count seven clean days anew, since a new excitement has arisen. Likewise, one who remarries his divorced wife must have her count seven clean days anew, even if he divorced her while she was pregnant or nursing and remarried her in that same state — due to excitement.
takeaways: Every woman marrying (even a minor or elderly woman) is obligated in counting seven clean days due to "blood of excitement," following the law of an actual niddah.
A postponed and then renewed marriage, and likewise remarrying a divorced wife, requires counting seven clean days anew (due to renewed excitement).

paragraphs: Hakkones et habbetula, boel beilat metzuvveh; v"p sheddam betulim shotet veyored, gomer biato veeno choshesh; abal leachar sheggamar biato, poresh atzmo mimmenna vehi temea, vaapillu lo matzea dam, temea, dechosheshin shemma yatza tippat dam vechapehu shikbat-zera, al-ken machaziqin otah kenidda gemura, kak katab mera"n za"l beshulchano hattahor; ak mvr"m za"l katab: veyesh meqillin im lo raata dam, venahagu lehaqel im lo gemar bia, raq heera bah velo raata dam, abal im ba aleha bia mammash, tzarik liprosh mimmenna "p shello raata dam, ad kan leshono. ubedibre haramba"m za"l, bepereq Adonai mehilkot issure bia meporash, digmar bia hu haknasat haebar lipnim min hillul, ayyen sham; vezeh yihyeh behaknasat kol haebar. vehinneh poh irenu bagdad y" nahagu lehaqel im lo raata dam; ak im yodea habbaal beatzmo sheasa gemar bia, en lehaqel, vetzarik liprosh mimmenna "p shello raata dam. ubeshabbat muttar libol habbetula, "p sheoseh chabbura.

clarification.explanation: One who marries a virgin performs "a union of mitzvah," and even though virginal blood is flowing, he completes the union without concern; but after completing the union, he separates from her, and she is considered impure even if no blood is found at all — since there is concern a drop of blood may have emerged and been covered by the semen, and therefore she is considered a complete niddah, as Maran ruled. The Rema is lenient: some are lenient if she did not see blood, and the lenient custom applies only if there was no completed union but merely partial contact without seeing blood; but if there was an actual completed union, one must separate from her even if she did not see blood. "Completed union" is defined by the Rambam as the full entry of the organ inside. In Baghdad the custom is to be lenient if she did not see blood, but if the husband himself knows there was a completed union, one should not be lenient and must separate from her. It is permitted to have intercourse with a virgin on the Sabbath, even though a wound (bruise) results from it.
takeaways: On the wedding night, after a completed union with a virgin, there is concern that blood emerged and was covered by semen, and she is considered a niddah even without visible blood.
In Baghdad the custom is to be lenient if she did not see blood, unless the husband knows for certain there was a completed union.
It is permitted to have intercourse with a virgin on the Sabbath, even though it causes bleeding (a bruise).

paragraphs: Hayyoledet - ben yaleda valad chay, ben met - temea tumat leda, shiba yamim lazzakar vearbaa asar lanneqeba, vezo hi tumat leda hakketubba battora. veyamim ellu deachar leda, "p shehem yeme tuma, olim lah leshiba neqiyyim im sapera bahem karauy, veshamera otam bishbil shiba neqiyyim; ubilbad shello titbol qodem y"d linqeba, ella tamtin ad lel t"v vetitbol. vekol zeh hu middina, ak yesh meqomot nohagim sheen tobelot tok arbaim yom lezakar ushemonim linqeba. upoh irenu bagdad y" yesh miqtzat nashim shennahagu bekak, abal rob hannashim lo nahagu bazeh, ella kol zeman shettireh atzmah sheyyekola laasot hepseq betahora achar z' lezakar vy"d linqeba, soperet z' neqiyyim vetobelet, ben lezakar, ben linqeba. velaken anachnu morim poh irenu: mi shennahag bearbaim ushemonim, yishshaer beminhago; mihu, im ellu hammachmirin bearbaim ushemonim qasheh alehem dabar zeh mechamat ezeh sibbot hekrechiyyut, yekolin laasot hattara al chumera zo, veaz yaasu keminhag rob hannashim shebbeir zo. vekatabti bs"d bitshuba bsh"q "rab-pealim", sheyyesh bazeh seper sapeqa vehu: sapeq keman deamar "minhag bistama, tolin betaut umebattelin leh"; veim timtze lomar halaka keman deamar "tolin begeder useyag" - shemma halaka keman deamar deal yede sheela muttar; usepeq sapeqa zeh hu mithappek; vekevan dehu midi derabbanan, samekinan al sepeq sepeqa zeh lehattir apillu beheka dekol anshe hair nohagim bekak, vekol shekken beheka derob hair lo nahagu bekak, deyesh lehattir leotam hammiut "y sheela, vekevan deen minhag qabua bair, have minhag yechidim. veayyen "teshuba meahaba", yoreh dea, teshuba shs"v, shekkatab dimtzuvveh lehattir minhag zeh "y sheela; veayyen "peleti", yeuyyan sham. vekatabti sham deap al gab deqayma lan: en mattirin hanneder ad sheyyachul - haynu davqa beneder, abal minhag mattirin qodem sheyyachul; ukemo shekkatab mahari"y y"sh za"l b"bet-yeuddeh", cheleq 'b, siman tz"z, vehebio beshiyyure beraka, ot z', yeuyyan sham. vekatabti od sham dedor hechadash shello nahagu adayin bechumra zo, yekolim linhog kerub anshe hair, "p sheimmotehem nahagu bezo hachumra shel arbaim ushemonim; veayyen "pitche-teshuba", siman ry"d, seip qatan d mah shekkatab beshem "zikron-yosep". veda daapillu otam shennahagu lehachmir bearbaim ushemonim, en lahem chumera zo ella beyoledet velo bemappelet; veayyen "sidre-tahora", siman qtz"d, seip qatan v', v"teshuba meahaba", cheleq b, shehebi dibre haggaon "chakam tzebi" za"l veqalleseh, yeuyyan sham. mihu, din tumat leda shehu shiba lazzakar vearbaa asar lanneqeba, yeshno gam bemappelet; vekol shehippila tok arbaim yom, kegon shebbarur lah ken mechamat shello shimmesha qodem, en noheg bah din tumat yoledet, ella dinah kishar niddot.

clarification.explanation: A woman who gives birth — whether to a living or a stillborn child — is impure with the impurity of childbirth: seven days for a male, fourteen days for a female. These days of impurity also count for her as the count of seven clean days, if she kept them properly, provided she does not immerse before the fourteenth day when giving birth to a female, but waits until the fifteenth night. In some places the custom is not to immerse within forty days of a male birth and eighty days of a female birth (an additional stringency, not by strict law), but most women in Baghdad did not follow this, immersing instead according to the basic law (seven/fourteen) as soon as they are able. One who follows the stringency of forty/eighty should remain in her practice, but if the stringency is difficult for her for compelling reasons, she may perform a "hatarah" on it and follow the practice of most women. And daughters of the new generation who have not yet followed this stringency may follow the practice of most people in the city, even though their mothers followed it, and they do not need a hatarah. This stringency (forty/eighty) applies only to a woman who gave birth and not to one who miscarried; but the basic law of the impurity of childbirth (seven/fourteen) applies also to a miscarriage if it is clear a fetus had formed. A miscarriage within forty days from the start of pregnancy is not considered at all the impurity of childbirth, and her law is that of an ordinary niddah.
takeaways: The impurity of childbirth: seven days for a male, fourteen for a female; these days count toward the seven clean days.

The stringency of waiting forty/eighty days is an additional custom (not by strict law), and may be released in case of difficulty; a daughter who has not yet followed it need not accept it, even if her mother did.
A miscarriage within forty days from the start of pregnancy is not the impurity of childbirth at all, but that of an ordinary niddah.

paragraphs: Ishah shehi bechezqat temea, asur lebalah labo aleha ad shettomar lo "tabalti"; veen tzarik shettomar lo bepeh male, ella kol sheaberu yamim sheepshar lah limnot velitbol, vehi baa veshekkaba etzlo, day bazeh; ukemo shekkatab harab "lechem vesimla", udelo keharab "chavvot-daat" za"l. veim huchzeqa nidda bishkenutah, kegon sherauha lobeshet begadim hamyuchadim lime niddatah, chashiba temea vadday. veim amera lebalah "temea ani", veachar kede dibbur amera "tehora ani", enah neemenet; veim natena ammatla lidbareha, neemenet; vaapillu shebbalah yodea middato haamatla - tzarik shettomar lo haamatla beperush; vela mehanne haamatla ella beheka deamera "temea ani" velo aseta maaseh, abal im labesha begadim hamyuchadim leniddatah, apillu amera amatla enah neemenet. upoh irenu bagdad en derek sheyyomru hannashim bepihem al tumatam, ella im ba limsor lah chepetz, mosheket yadah veenah meqabbalto; veim ba lelek betziddah liga bah, hi marcheqet atzmah, umizzeh yabin shehi temea; laken im aseta kak, tzarik shettomar haamatla beperush.

clarification.explanation: A woman presumed impure (a niddah) — her husband is forbidden to be intimate with her until she tells him "I have immersed" — and there is no need for her to say this explicitly; rather, whenever enough days have passed for her to count and immerse, and she comes and lies down with him, this suffices. A woman presumed to be a niddah in her neighborhood (for example, seen wearing clothes designated for her days of niddah) — is considered impure with certainty. If she said "I am impure" and immediately afterward said "I am pure," she is not believed, unless she gives a reason ("amtala") for her words — in which case she is believed, and even though her husband already knows the reason on his own, she must state the reason to him explicitly. An amtala helps only if she said "I am impure" alone and performed no accompanying act; but if she has already worn the clothes designated for her niddah, an amtala does not help. In Baghdad it is not customary for women to state their impurity verbally, but rather they signal it through behavior (for example, pulling back their hand when an object is handed to them, or keeping their distance) — in such a case, if she wishes to retract, she must state the amtala explicitly.
takeaways: A woman presumed impure is forbidden to her husband until she indicates (explicitly or by action) that she has immersed.
A contradictory statement (impure-then-pure) requires an amtala (explanation) to be believed, and this does not help if she has already behaviorally shown she is impure.

paragraphs: "p shebbalah muttar lehityached immah bime tumatah, mikkol maqom lo yischoq immah bidbarim hammargilim leerva kol zeman shello tabela; vaapillu lizroq chepetz mizzeh lazeh asur; veim yesh beyadah ner doleq, vehabbaal madliq sigarya shel tabbaq min hashshalhebet, o madliq ner shebbeyado min ner shebbeyadah - oser harab "yad-eliyyahu" za"l, veken mhrsh"q za"l b"sheyare-tahora" name asar bazeh. veim yesh notza al begadeha, vehu nopeach lahasirah berucha piv - oser harab "minchat-yaaqob" za"l; vahagam dehaacharonim hittiru binpicha, nakon lehachmir; mihu vadday asur shettanip alayv bimnipa lehabi lo rucha qar, ki zeh have debar chibba "p sheenah nogaat bo.

Veken en okelin al shulchan echad ella im ken yesh shinnuy, sheyyihyeh shum dabar mapsiq ben qeara shello liqara shellah, kegon lechem sheen okelim mimmennu, o qanqan sheen shotin bo, kede sheyyihyeh hekker bazeh. veyesh mattirin beheka dehi meshanna meqomah, sheenah yoshebet bemaqom shergila lesheb bizman tahoratah; veken yesh mattirin im kol echad okel miqqeara shello; veyesh mattirin im yesh od acherim mesubbin al hashshulchan; veal-ken yesh lismok lehattir bitnaim ellu bimqomot shergilim bekak, veqasheh alehem meod haddabar hazzeh shettokal hi lebaddah chutz lashshulchan. veotam sheddarkam lehannicha kol habbasar biqara gedola veken kol hammaraq biqara gedola veken haorez, vehem yesh lahem kol echad qeara lepanayv, venotelin kol echad veechad min hamsubbin bekap min haqqearot haggedolot umannichin baqqearot shellipnehem, veaz okelim kol echad veechad miqqeara shellepanayv, shari bikhay gavna, dachashib bazeh kol echad okel biqara bipne atzmo. gam yizzaher habbaal shello yishteh mishshiyyure hakkos sheshshateta hi mimmennu, veken lo yokal mishshiyyure maakol shellah; veim hipsiq adam acher benehem, o shehuraq mikkeli el keli, apillu shehuchzar lakkeli harishon, muttar. vedavqa habbaal asur lishtot veleekol mishshiyyurim shellah, abal hi mutteret leekol velishtot mishshiyyurim shello. veim akela veshiyyera o shateta veshiyyera vehaleka lah, muttar lebalah leekol velishtot hashshiyyurin, dekevan shehaleka lah en kan chibba. veim ba habbaal leekol hashshiyyurin achar sheakela, vehitchil leekol, veqodem sheggamar akilato baa, muttar lesayyem akilato bepaneha; ken heela haggaon mahara"m b"yd-eliyyahu"; veken heeleti ana abada bsh"q "rab-pealim", vehebeti besiyyata dishmayya kamma reayot bazeh lehattir.

clarification.explanation: Although a husband is permitted to be secluded with his wife during her days of impurity, he is forbidden to play with her in ways that lead to intimacy as long as she has not immersed — even throwing an object back and forth between them is forbidden. Some forbid even passing fire (lighting a cigarette or candle from one held in her hand). Blowing a feather off her clothes — although some are lenient, it is proper to be stringent. Waving a fan to bring him air — is certainly forbidden, since this is an act of affection even without contact. Eating at one table is permitted only on condition there is a distinguishing "heker" (a marker) — such as an item they do not eat from placed between the dishes; some permit it if she changes her seating place, or if each eats from his own separate dish, or if there are additional people at the table — and one may rely on these conditions when needed. If food is served in large shared bowls but each person takes their own portion into a separate dish, this is permitted, since it is considered that each eats from his own dish. The husband may not drink from the remainder of her cup or eat from the remainder of her food (due to the affection involved), but she is permitted to eat from his remainder. If someone else interposed between them, or the food was transferred from vessel to vessel, it is permitted. If she finished eating and left, the husband may eat from her leftovers; and if he began eating from the leftovers and she came in the meantime, he may continue eating in front of her.
takeaways: It is forbidden to play, throw objects, or perform acts of affection with one's wife during her days of impurity, even without direct contact.
Eating at one table is permitted only with a distinguishing marker between the dishes, or other lenient conditions (a different seat, separate dishes, others present).
The husband may not eat or drink from her leftovers (unless she has already left), but she is permitted to eat from his.

paragraphs: Lo yesheb bammitta hamyuchedet lah apillu shello bepaneha, vekol shekken deasur lishon al mittatah; vehu haddin deasur lesheb al karim hamyuchadim lah, abal muttar liga bahem, vaapillu besadin shealayv haddam muttar liga. vehi mutteret lesheb al mittato, abal lishon al mittato asur. veim yesh sapsal arok sheeno mechubbar lakkotel, umitnadned kesheyyoshebin alayv, asur lesheb alayv shenehem "p sheen nogeim zeh bazeh. v"p demera"n za"l bebet yosep katab: chumera zo dishibat hassapsal, shamati shennohagim bah haashkenazzim, abal hasseparaddim lo nahagu bah - hinneh hamminhag pashut beirenu miqqodem qidmatah shello lesheb alayv shenehem apillu en nogeim zeh bazeh; veyesh mattirim im yesh adam acher yosheb umapsiq benehem. veim hu kabed harbeh sheeno mitnadned, muttarim lesheb alayv apillu en adam mapsiq benehem, kol sheen nogeim zeh bazeh. veasur lesheb al machtzelet chadasha apillu en nogeim zeh bazeh, mippene shemmitnadnedet. velo yeleku shenehem baagala achat o bispina qetanna, im holekim bishbil tiyyul; abal im holekim letzorek, muttar apillu im lebaddam yoshebim, veraq shello yihyu nogeim zeh bazeh.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden for the husband to sit on her designated bed even in her absence, and all the more so it is forbidden to sleep on it. It is likewise forbidden to sit on her designated pillows, though it is permitted to touch them, even to touch a sheet with blood on it. She, by contrast, is permitted to sit on his bed (though not to sleep on it). A long bench not attached to the wall that wobbles when sat upon — both are forbidden to sit on it together, even without touching each other, since the wobbling creates a kind of closeness; the Baghdad custom was to be stringent about this even without contact. If the bench is heavy and does not wobble, both may sit on it as long as they do not touch. A new (wobbling) mat is likewise forbidden. One should not ride together in a cart or small boat for pleasure (due to the wobbling and closeness), but for a necessary purpose it is permitted, provided they do not touch each other.
takeaways: It is forbidden to sit or sleep on her designated bed or pillows (and conversely, she may sit but not sleep on his bed).
A wobbling bench or new mat is forbidden for both together, even without contact; a heavy, non-wobbling bench is permitted.

paragraphs: Lo yistakkel bimqomot hamkussim shebbah apillu baaqebah, abal muttar lehistakkel bimqomot haggeluyim shebbah v"p shenneheneh biriyyato. velo timzog lo kos yayin bepanayv, velo tannichennu lepanayv al hashshulchan, ella tannichennu al haaretz o al hassapsal, o timserennu leadam acher; veshello bepanayv mutteret lehannicho al hashshulchan gam ken. veyesh machmirim gam biqara shel maakol hamyuchedet lo davqa, shello tannichenna lepanayv al hashshulchan. vetob lachush ledibrehem heka deepshar, veayyen "chakemat-adam". ukeshem sheasur lah limzog lo hakkos lepanayv, ken hu asur limzog lah; veken asur lishloach lah kos shel beraka, veken name asur lishloach lah kos hamyuchad lah, kegon lel pesach.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden for the husband to look at the covered parts of her body, even at her heel, but it is permitted to look at the exposed parts even if he derives pleasure from it. She should not pour him a cup of wine in his presence nor place it before him on the table, but rather place it on the floor, on a bench, or hand it through another person; in his absence she is permitted to place it on the table. Some are stringent also regarding her serving him his food dish, that she not place it before him on the table, and it is good to be concerned for this where possible. Just as it is forbidden for her to pour him a cup in his presence, it is likewise forbidden for him to pour her one; and it is likewise forbidden to send her a cup of blessing, or a cup designated for her (such as on Passover night).
takeaways: It is forbidden to look at the covered parts of her body; permitted for the exposed parts.
Serving a cup of wine or a food dish in his/her presence is forbidden in both directions; permitted in the other's absence.

paragraphs: Asur lehatztzia lo mittato bepanayv. vedavqa perisat hassedinim vehamkasseh, shehu derek chibba; abal karim ukesatot, shehem torach veenam derek chibba, shari. vekatab harab "lechem vesimla", ki ledaat kamma poseqim gam zeh asur, ayyen sham; venireh li denakon lehachmir bazeh heka deepshar; vekol zeh davqa bepanayv, abal shello bepanayv, muttar ap al pi shehu yodea shehi hammatztzaat otam, shari. veasur leharicha bibsamim shellah ap al pi shehesiratam mealeha; vekatab birke yosep remez laddabar: "suga bashshoshannim" - sheoseh seyag gam bashshoshannim. veasur lishmoa qol zemer shellah; veayyen "lechem vesimla", seip qatan k. upoh irenu minhag hannashim lezammer lehayyeled beqol naim kede sheyyashen ukede shello yibkeh, vetzarik lehizzaher bazeh im ishto nidda; ak im hayyeled bokeh harbeh, vetzarik lezammer zeh shemmelummad bekak, veen maqom labbaal lelek sham, nireh deyesh lehaqel. veasur latet lipne balah qiton shel mayim vehakkelim sheyyirchatz bahem panayv yadayv veraglayv, mippene shehu derek chibba, veen hammayim tzonenim, vekannizkar bashsha"k beshem rabbenu yona za"l. vekol azharot hannizkarot leel, hem shayyakim gam beshiba neqiyyim, kol zeman shello tabela adayin. vehammazhir vehannizhar, alehem tabo birkat tob.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden for her to make (arrange) his bed in his presence, specifically the spreading of sheets and the cover, which are an act of affection; but arranging pillows and cushions, which is effort and not an act of affection, is permitted — although some authorities are stringent about this as well, and it is proper to be stringent where possible. In his absence, she is fully permitted to make his bed, even if he knows she is the one who made it. It is forbidden for him to smell her perfumes even after she has already removed them from herself — and a hint to this, the "Berachi Yosef" wrote: "a hedge of roses" — that one makes a fence even around a pleasant thing like roses. It is forbidden for him to hear the sound of her singing voice. In the case of a crying infant whom the mother sings to in order to put to sleep, and the husband has no choice but to be present — it appears one may be lenient. It is forbidden for her to hand him a water pitcher and washing vessel before him, for his hands and feet, since this is an act of affection. All these warnings apply also during the days of the seven clean days, as long as she has not yet immersed.
takeaways: It is forbidden for her to make his bed in his presence (spreading sheets — an act of affection; pillows — permitted, though with difficulty), and forbidden for him to smell her perfume or hear her singing voice.
The hint to the prohibition on scent comes from the verse "a hedge of roses" — that a fence is made even around a pleasant thing.
An exceptional case: a crying infant the mother soothes by singing — there is room to be lenient.
All these warnings apply also during the seven clean days, until immersion.
